searchText: <@!203220829473996800> is that the correct way of bencharking? somehow on my PC (i9-9980XE overclocked and watercooled), FFT is almost 2x slower than on yours Afk, but will look into that. Check which build tag you're using. And G1 or F_r FFT. And there's another special-purpose extension FFT. <@!570268431522201601> So for a F_r FFT scale 15, you're getting 44 ms, using Kilic BLS? With Herumi BLS, I get 79 ms. Using Kilic BLS, I get 26 ms. (on old laptop, `i7-6700HQ @ 8x 3.5GHz`). I'll re-run the latest code and see if anything changed significantly. And will try a different machine. us I would recommend you set the Go bench time param, to run it 10 seconds (that's what I did), instead of the default single second benchmark it didn't seem to change anything And what do you get with herumi BLS? FYI my own implementation is somehow 6 times faster herumi There's another 2x waiting for Go-kate in open PR Kilic BLS + use mont. red. multiplication you can use this to test my code ``` git clone -b kate-poly-commitment https://github.com/mratsim/constantine nim c -r --debugger:native -d:danger --outdir:build/ --hints:off --warnings:off --verbosity:0 research/kate/fft.nim ``` assuming you have the latest Nim stable (1.4.2) or devel So your Herumi BLS benchmarks look slightly better than mine, but you've a better CPU too, no surprise there But surprised about kilic BLS being 2x slower for you yes that's why I want to make sure I didn't forget something silly like compiling the benchmark in release mode how to compile just fft_fr_bench_test.go? I can run it under VTune to find the perf bottlenecks Not sure about vtune, go has its own tooling I used a little for go-kate. VTune works for go, i used it to trace bottlenecks in "addchain" iirc. but I don't know the first thing about compiling go binaries :p I just used go get 😉 fyi, just tried on my new pc, and getting 41 ms (fft f_r, scale 15) with kilic BLS. Will boot old laptop and check what's up. Regression maybe? Or just lucky platform choice? Hmm That's on a `AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core @ 32x 3.4GHz` (core count doesn't matter though, I didn't parallelize it yet) Also, let's move to DM before we spam this channel too much Update for others, after a bunch more benchmarks: my laptop just runs Kilic BLS better than the ryzen PC. Different architecture optimizations, and meanwhile the FFT code by <@!570268431522201601> has great performance on my ryzen.
